QF.id: Income, Residential Status, Five Heads of Income_1

question.text: Mr. Arjun, an Indian citizen working in Dubai, was present in India for 125 days during PY 2024-25 and 370 days during the 4 preceding years. His Indian income for the year is Rs. 18 lakh. Additionally, he was a resident of India in at least 2 of the 10 preceding previous years AND his cumulative stay in India during the 7 preceding previous years was 800 days. What is his residential status?

explanation.text: The Logic: Mr. Arjun is an Indian citizen visiting India. Because his Indian income exceeds Rs. 15 lakh, the 120-day relaxed threshold applies. He stayed 125 days (>120) in PY 2024-25 and 370 days (>365) in the 4 preceding years, so he is a Resident under s.6(1)(c). For ROR vs RNOR: a person is RNOR only if (a) he was Non-Resident in 9 of the 10 preceding previous years, OR (b) his cumulative stay in India during the 7 preceding previous years was 729 days or less. The stem states he was Resident in at least 2 of the 10 preceding years (so condition (a) fails) AND 800 days in the 7 preceding years (so condition (b) fails). Neither RNOR limb is satisfied, so he is ROR by default (option B). The Trap: Option A ignores the 120-day rule. Option C picks RNOR without verifying that neither RNOR limb is satisfied. Option D invokes deemed-resident provisions that do not apply here. In the original ambiguous version the stem did not supply the 9-of-10-year or 7-year-day-count facts, so ROR vs RNOR could not be determined. Note: The original question was ambiguous because the stem omitted the 9-out-of-10-year residency facts and the 7-year-day-count fact required by p.139-141 of NISM Series X-B to distinguish ROR from RNOR. The stem has been augmented with those facts so option B is uniquely correct. Source: NISM Series X-B (Investment Adviser Level 2), pp.139-141.
